kerberos: Add TgtRenewalScheduler class TgtRenewalScheduler is responsible for scheduling automatic Kerberos ticket-granting-ticket (TGT) renewals. Usually, TGTs are valid for 8-10 hours and can be renewed periodically for a week or 2, which refreshes the validity lifetime each time until the renewal lifetime limit is hit. TgtRenewalScheduler schedules renewal tasks. If the ticket lifetime is 10 hours, it schedules automatic renewals after 6h0m, 8h24m, 9h21m, 9h44m, 9h53m and 9h 57m. If all these attempts failed, it will send a notification that the ticket is about to expire. If the ticket was already expired, e.g. after waking up from a suspended state, it sends out a notification that the ticket has already expired. The class is not used yet. This is done in a follow-up CL. BUG=chromium:952242 TEST=Unit test Change-Id: Ice4ceac8432b6055098e2773ac4baa11632e3bcf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1680417 Tested-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org>

kerberos: Automatically renew Kerberos tickets Uses a TgtRenewalScheduler for each Kerberos account to automatically renew Kerberos tickets. If renewal fails, the code attempts to acquire a fresh ticket if the login password or a previously remembered password are available. If that fails as well, it emits a KerberosTicketExpiring notification 3 minutes before a ticket expires, so Chrome can pop up a notification. BUG=chromium:952242 TEST=Enable KerberosEnabled policy, go to chrome:settings/kerberosAccounts, add an account (e.g. using a chromeadm-lab.com account), add ticket_lifetime=10m to the configuration. Unplug network. Wait 7 minutes. You should eventually see a notification to refresh the ticket. With network plugged in, the ticket should renew and there should be not notification. device: led: probe the maximum value of brightness from ectool Previously in led.py, we assume the maximum value of brightness from the 'ectool led <name> <color>=<value>' command is 255. The actual maximum value may be different, e.g. 100. Using value larger than the maximum value is an unspecified behavior. On eve, it modulo the input value by the actual maximum value. In this case, the result is unwanted. This CL probes the maximum value of brightness using 'ectool led <name> query'. Also 'ectool led <name> <color>' set the brightness to 255, which always fails on devices with range check, e.g. nami. This CL makes brightness in LED.SetColor equal to 100 if not specified.
